mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average by more than 10% indicates a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when HOUST jumps above its 6-month moving average by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month moving averages signals robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which reduces immediate consumption demand and pressures corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.
